issues.description: Same-rank terminal records can overwrite newer terminal records, so an older completed/failed snapshot can silently replace later job data.
The unchanged check ignores user, partition, submit, start, alloc_cpus, gpus, and exit_code, so corrected accounting data may never be persisted.
Negative AllocCPUS and GPU counts are accepted, which can create negative CPU/GPU-hour reports.
Timezone-aware timestamps are accepted and stored as raw ISO text, but later SQL comparisons treat them lexicographically instead of chronologically.
Report filters, MAX reference time, and trailing windows compare timestamp strings directly, producing incorrect results when offsets or mixed timestamp forms exist.
Unknown Slurm states default to terminal rank, so valid intermediate states such as requeue/configuration variants can block later non-terminal updates.
Rows with empty user, empty partition, or no submit/start/end reference time are accepted, causing blank report groups or silently unreportable jobs.
All database opens create the parent directory, database, and schema, so read-only report commands can mask a wrong path by creating an empty database.
The schema has no user_version or migration path, making future schema changes unsafe for existing installed databases.
Database directory and file permissions rely entirely on process umask, which can expose local job accounting data on shared systems.
Report commands do not handle sqlite errors, so corrupt or inaccessible databases produce raw tracebacks instead of actionable CLI errors.
